bib.title: Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v1); published MLSys 2023 per caller

question: Can activation memory in large transformer training be cut enough to avoid most of the 30-40% overhead of full activation recomputation?
hypothesis: Sequence parallelism plus selective recomputation of cheap-to-recompute attention internals removes most recomputation cost without extra communication.
contributions: Sequence parallelism combined with tensor parallelism, dividing layer-norm and dropout activations along the sequence dimension
Selective activation recomputation of the attention core (QK^T, softmax, softmax dropout, attention over V)
Approximate per-layer and total activation memory formulas
Evaluation on 22B to 1T parameter models on A100 GPUs

method.summary: Derives activation memory per transformer layer, adds sequence parallelism (g/g-bar all-gather/reduce-scatter conjugates replacing tensor-parallel all-reduce) and recomputes only the attention core, then measures per-layer time and end-to-end iteration time for 22B, 175B, 530B and 1T GPT-style models with tensor parallel 8.
method.task: Large transformer pretraining systems efficiency (activation memory and throughput)

training.precision: mixed precision (16-bit activations assumed in memory formulas; logits 32-bit)
training.hardware: Selene supercomputer; nodes of 8 NVIDIA 80GB A100 GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch, eight 200Gbps HDR Infiniband HCAs per node; 2240 A100 GPUs for the 530B data-parallel run

other.note: Throughput benchmarks, not convergence training; no data parallelism except one 8-way DP run of the 530B model

metrics.name: Activation memory
metrics.definition: Percentage of memory vs tensor-parallel baseline (Eq 2)

metrics.name: Per-layer overhead
metrics.definition: Extra forward+backward time vs no-recompute baseline

metrics.name: MFU
metrics.definition: Model FLOPs per second divided by accelerator peak (312 TFLOPs for A100), after Chowdhery et al.

metrics.name: HFU
metrics.definition: Hardware FLOPs per second divided by peak

eval.protocol: Single measurement per configuration; no repeats or variance reported

availability.code: Megatron-LM and NeMo-Megatron (stated as will be available)

results.claim: Sequence parallelism plus selective recomputation cut activation memory about 5x versus the tensor-parallel baseline, to under 20%.
results.setup: 22B to 1T models, tensor parallel 8, s=2048, relative to Eq 2 baseline
results.quote: combined provide a 5x reduction bringing the memory requirements to under 20%

results.claim: 530B model on 2240 A100 GPUs reaches 54.2% MFU versus 42.1% with full recomputation.
results.quote: we achieve a Model Flops Utilization of 54.2%, which is 29% faster than the 42.1% we achieve

results.claim: Throughput improves 29.0% to 32.1% over full recomputation across 22B to 1T models.
results.quote: provide between 29.0% and 32.1% improvement in the throughput

results.claim: 1T model reaches 56.3% MFU and 57.0% HFU; iteration time 71.49 s vs 94.42 s with full recompute.
results.setup: 1T model, 512 GPUs, TP 8, PP 64, selective + sequence parallel
results.quote: we reach a MFU and HFU of 56.3% and 57.0%
results.table: Table 5, row 1T, columns Model FLOPs Utilization / Hardware FLOPs Utilization

results.claim: Execution-time overhead of recomputation falls by over 90%; per-layer overhead is 2% for 530B and 1T vs 36% for full recompute.
results.quote: the overhead is just 2%, compared to 36% overhead for full recompute

results.claim: On one 22B layer, combined techniques cut overhead to 4% versus 39% for full-layer recompute.
results.table: Table 4, row Selective + Sequence, column Overhead (%)
results.note: Full-layer recompute overhead 39% exceeds expected 33% due to overlap of all-reduce with weight gradient

results.claim: Per-layer activation memory with tensor + sequence parallelism is Eq 1 divided by t: sbh/t (34 + 5as/h).
results.setup: 16-bit activations, dropout masks 1 byte; no pipeline correction
results.quote: The above equation is now Equation 1 divided by the tensor parallel size.

results.claim: Selective recomputation saves 70% (GPT-3) and 65% (MT-NLG) of activation memory at 2.7% and 1.6% FLOPs overhead.
results.quote: we can save 70% and 65% of the
results.note: Quote spans a line break in the source; 2.7% and 1.6% FLOPs overheads are in the following sentence

results.claim: Full activation recomputation incurs 30-40% execution time overhead in the authors' runs.
Microbatch-level recomputation adds only +0.7% (175B) and +0.4% (530B) MFU.
results.setup: 175B MFU 52.3%, 530B 56.4%, vs sequence parallel + selective baseline

limits: No data parallelism in most evaluations, so batch sizes are far below real training; authors say the 8-way DP run adds little overhead (MFU 56.0% to 54.2%).
Comparison with ZeRO/offloading is declared out of scope and left for future work.
Memory fragmentation and first-pipeline-stage memory pressure left unresolved.
Single measurements; no variance or seeds reported; no convergence or accuracy study.
Activation formulas assume 16-bit storage and ignore small buffers; hardware limited to A100.

terms.definition: checkpoint and recompute only parts of each transformer layer that take up a considerable amount of memory but are not computationally expensive to recompute
partition the non-tensor-parallel regions (layer-norm, dropout) along the sequence dimension
checkpoint activations at transformer layer boundaries and recompute the rest in the backward pass
